newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-RUBIN WINS AT ATLANTA OLYMPIC VENUE A YEAR LATER.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RUBIN WINS AT ATLANTA OLYMPIC VENUE A YEAR LATER.

text.p: A year after being forced to miss the Atlanta Games with a wrist injury, Chanda Rubin finally made it to the Olympic tennis venue and turned in a gold medal performance on Monday.
Rubin needed just 52 minutes to overpower Czech veteran Helena Sukova 6-1 6-2 in the opening round of the U.S. Women's Hardcourt Championships.

Fifth seed Amanda Coetzer of South Africa, who has entered every North American hardcourt tournament leading up to next week's U.S. Open, also powered her way into the second round with a 6-1 6-2 thrashing of American Linda Wild.
Seventh seed Ruxandra Dragomir of Romania joined the pair in the second round with a 6-3 6-3 victory over Anne-Gaelle Sidot of France.
There was one seeded casualty at Stone Mountain Park Monday when Sandrine Testud of France downed eighth seed Karina Habsudova of Slovakia 6-3 6-1.

The top four seeds -- Jana Novotna, Monica Seles, who is coming off back-to-back titles, French Open champion Iva Majoli and Lindsay Davenport, who won Olympic singles gold here last summer -- all received first-round byes.
When Rubin faced Sukova three weeks ago in San Diego, she was forced to withdraw in the second set of a tight match with an ankle injury.
On Monday it was all Rubin, who dropped just six points over the first five games.
"I just started off better and served better and I was steadier off the ground," Rubin said of the rematch.
"She likes to attack and be the aggressor, and I just wanted to keep the ball deep early in the point until I got my shot. I felt like I did that better than I did in San Diego."
But like most everyone else playing this event, getting ready for the U.S. Open is the prime concern.
"I'm just looking to use this week to try to play some good tennis, get some good matches in, keep improving and go from there," Rubin said.
